destination.title: Antibrane backreaction and metastability
destination.question: Under which source, boundary and approximation conditions can antibranes in flux backgrounds form admissible metastable configurations once polarization, interactions and brane–flux decay are considered?
destination.summary: Regularity, preservation of the ultraviolet theory, polarization equilibria and dynamical stability are separate tests. The supplied evidence supports competing questions and qualified arguments, not a common verdict.

systems: Anti-D2 and anti-M2 in their specified CGLP settings
Other explicitly specified antibrane and polarized-shell configurations
targets: Admissible infrared behavior and ultraviolet matching
regimes: Channel-specific polarization and perturbative versus nonlinear analyses
assumptions: Necessary gluing conditions alone do not establish a complete stable solution
conventions: Ordinary source singularities and additional flux divergences are distinguished
D5, NS5, oblique and M5 channels are not interchangeable
excludes: Automatic extension of a smeared obstruction to every localized polarized state
Universal failure or success of compact uplift

evidence.text: Can singular fluxes near anti-branes be interpreted as the stationary description of an instability, resolved by time-dependent flux attraction followed by brane-flux annihilation? The intended application is anti-D3 metastability in the Klebanov–Strassler throat.

evidence.text: Does antibrane backreaction enhance brane-flux annihilation enough to remove the KPV metastable state, and can antibranes consequently provide controlled supersymmetry breaking and uplift? sources.title: Assessing a candidate IIA dual to metastable supersymmetry-breaking

evidence.text: Compute a static D2 probe's DBI plus Wess–Zumino force and calibrate boundary conditions by adding ordinary BPS D2 branes. Opposite shifts of g2 and g3 change the Maxwell D2 charge while preserving the S4 flux and reproduce the expected smeared-brane warp-factor singularity.

sources.title: Resolving anti-brane singularities through time-dependence

evidence.text: A charged-fluid analogy separates flux pressure, attraction toward opposite charge, and annihilation. It contrasts a finite-density stationary metastable configuration with increasing clumping that removes the annihilation barrier.

sources.title: Anti-D3 Branes: Singular to the bitter end

evidence.text: A supplementary global argument rewrites the f,k,F sector using a nonnegative reduced Lagrangian whose zero occurs at vanishing ξ₁,f,k,F⁻. The remaining fields are treated as free functions subject to regularity conditions; the argument is explicitly cautioned because the equations are singular in the infrared.

sources.title: Giant Tachyons in the Landscape

evidence.text: Expand flux near the North Pole, extract its designated (1,2) and (3,0) components to determine m′/m, and combine this with the rescaling invariant λ=a_2a_4/a_3² to infer NS5 and oblique quadratic terms.

sources.title: Fatal attraction: more on decaying anti-branes

evidence.text: Insert a flux-clumping parameter λ into the Abelian NS5 DBI plus Chern-Simons action and extract a potential for its polar angle ψ. The B6 coupling supplies the λ-dependent force, while quantized F3 flux fixes the retained KS expression for C2.

sources.title: Perturbative decay of anti-branes in flux backgrounds due to space time instabilities

evidence.text: Compare the homogeneous energy E0=L V(p,ψmin) with two-region configurations, L=L1+L2, p1<p<p2, and p1L1+p2L2=pL. Choose the NS5 position to minimize the local potential separately in each region.

Does a DSB sector that is consistent in isolation remain stable inside the near-horizon geometry of many regular branes?

destination.title: Inflationary potentials and coupled throats
destination.question: How do bulk deformations, warping and brane backreaction determine inflationary potentials or the evolution of homologically related throats?
destination.summary: D3-probe potentials, five-brane monodromy constructions and post-annihilation throat evolution retain separate fine questions.

sources.title: D3-brane Potentials from Fluxes in AdS/CFT

evidence.text: What is the leading position-dependent potential of a probe D3-brane in a warped conifold throat when supersymmetry breaking and moduli stabilization in the compact bulk induce general ultraviolet deformations, including nonperturbative D7-brane effects?

sources.title: Brane-Antibrane Backreaction in Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Does direct five-brane backreaction invalidate the localization and warping assumptions of axion monodromy models containing an NS5/anti-NS5 pair on distant homologous two-cycles? The paper approaches this through a calculable D5/anti-D5 interaction potential.

sources.title: Bifid Throats for Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Can an explicit local geometry and holographic gauge theory realize the bifid throat needed for five-brane axion monodromy, including homologous infrared two-cycles and a quantitative treatment of five-brane-pair backreaction with warping?

sources.title: Brane/flux annihilation in double-throat system

evidence.text: How does brane/flux annihilation change flux distributions and relative geometry in two homologically related throats, and under what endpoint conditions does it restore their equivalence?

sources.title: D3-brane Potentials from Fluxes in AdS/CFT

evidence.text: AdS/CFT operator matching and supersymmetry-breaking spurions organize the field-theory interpretation. D7 gaugino-bilinear couplings are varied as localized sources for the bulk flux equation.

sources.title: Brane-Antibrane Backreaction in Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: One-loop vacuum energies are extracted from annulus partition functions. The calculation sums spin structures, applies modular transformations and Poisson resummation, and uses orbifold and Chan–Paton projections to separate untwisted D3 contributions from partially twisted D5 contributions.

sources.title: Bifid Throats for Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Use toric web splittings to identify complex deformations, and dimer diagrams with zig-zag homology classes to construct quivers, fractional-brane ranks, Higgsings, and the surviving two-cycle charges.

sources.title: Brane/flux annihilation in double-throat system

evidence.text: Use the reviewed GVW superpotential, warped complex-structure metric, and the combined KS plus antibrane potential to determine shifts of the stabilized deformation modulus z.

sources.title: D3-brane Potentials from Fluxes in AdS/CFT

evidence.text: A Green's-function solution separates the flux-sourced potential from arbitrary harmonic contributions. Four-dimensional curvature is included through a modified-Bessel solution and an iterative Green's-function expansion.

sources.title: D3-brane Potentials from Fluxes in AdS/CFT

evidence.text: Closed IASD three-forms are built from the Kähler form J, holomorphic three-form Ω and scalar harmonic functions. Angular harmonic analysis determines radial exponents and the dual operator spectrum.

sources.title: Inflation in warped geometries

evidence.text: Can local D3-probe dynamics compute corrections to the brane–antibrane inflation η-problem from conformal symmetry breaking in warped KKLT throats, and can those corrections permit η ≪ 1?
